items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: you’re certainly going in the right direction here with people like Milt Fillius and what you’re doing

ctx.x: Yeah, because we’re getting a couple of generations away from that music now, so it gets harder and harder. If the generation right after the music didn’t get it, what makes you think the next one’s going to? Well you spoke pretty eloquently earlier on about the fact that every generation has its own thing, has to find its own way. I wish we could find a way that the music could be made available, perhaps more available than it is, so that they could make their own choice. © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

Well I think that you’re going in the right direction, you’re certainly going in the right direction here with people like Milt Fillius and what you’re doing, Monk. I think certainly. You can encourage. There are a lot of people at Bob’s age group who are more than happy to come on to your campus and spend a month doing an Artist in Residency. They are sitting around not necessarily wanting to be running for gigs all the time, but they would be happy to pass on their legacy and to come in and be articulate and…
